new_events.actor: Kuwait Oil Tanker Company / VLCC Al Funtas
new_events.summary: Delayed UKMTO-derived maritime reporting said the Kuwait Oil Tanker Company VLCC Al Funtas was struck during an evening Strait of Hormuz transit. A fire was extinguished, the crew was reported safe and the vessel continued underway. Attacker, projectile type and full damage extent were not established in the collected public reporting.

The United States announced sanctions on 13 individuals and entities that U.S. authorities said supported Iranian weapons or component procurement, including targets associated with Russia, China, Hong Kong, Pakistan and Iran. The sanctions action is established; procurement allegations remain attributed to the U.S. government and no operational effect is inferred.

existing_event_updates.summary: Qatar publicly confirmed continued shuttle diplomacy and message exchange aimed at finding common ground after the U.S. rejection of Iran's seven-day proposal. No agreement to reopen Hormuz was established by the evidence horizon, and a new direct U.S.-Iran exchange was not established.

The Al Funtas incident adds a new physical-risk datapoint to the Hormuz security record. It does not by itself supersede the existing Kpler/LSEG traffic series or establish normalization/reversal of the broader traffic trend.

Reuters reported before the Sep.30 midnight ET evidence horizon that the final U.S. troops had departed their remaining Iraq base, ending the U.S.-led Operation Inherent Resolve presence in Iraq. The Pentagon said targeted training and intelligence support would continue. This supersedes the prior 'set to leave by Sep.30' posture with completion, without adopting actor claims about strategic victory or future militia effects.

economic_energy_updates.summary: The U.S. government offered energy companies loans of up to 40 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, described as the remaining U.S. tranche of the coordinated IEA emergency-release program. The offer is established; actual borrowing was not established at the horizon.

Public reporting said Washington urged European governments to draw down emergency diesel inventories amid continuing Iran-war and Hormuz supply pressure. EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen confirmed discussions while saying no decision had been made on additional releases.
